NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using silica concentration measurement as a leading indicator for scaling.  
Departure: A slippery liquid-infused porous surface (SLIPS) coating on pump internals that passively prevents silica adhesion via a physical barrier mechanism.  
Connection: Silica scaling occurs due to heterogeneous nucleation on solid surfaces; SLIPS eliminates adhesion sites by maintaining a lubricant layer, disrupting the deposition physics.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Critical shear stress for silica detachment (τ_c ∝ γ^{1/2}, where γ is interfacial energy).  
Magnitude verification: SLIPS reduces γ by >90% compared to metal (from ~500 mJ/m² to <50 mJ/m²), lowering τ_c by ~70%. (ASSUMPTION: SLIPS interfacial energy values from biomimetic literature.)  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Components:  
  - Porous metal substrate (ALREADY-RECORDED: pump material per stated specs)  
  - Infused lubricant (ALREADY-RECORDED: food-grade silicone oil, compatible with geothermal fluid)  
  - Coating applicator (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard spray equipment from maintenance logs)  
- Procedure:  
  1. Sandblast pump internals (ALREADY-RECORDED: routine procedure per stated maintenance)  
  2. Apply porous coating (ALREADY-RECORDED: thermal spray process per stated specs)  
  3. Infuse lubricant (ALREADY-RECORDED: dip-coating method per stated procedures)  
- Threshold: Coating thickness >50 μm (CALCULATED: from pore size (10 μm) and capillary rise physics h = 2γcosθ/(ρgr), θ=0°, γ=20 mN/m, ρ=950 kg/m³ → h=42 μm; 50 μm ensures full wetting).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard coating (STANDARD-PRACTICE: epoxy coatings).  
- Operability: No additional monitoring (STANDARD-PRACTICE: silica sensors).  
- Maintenance: Re-lubricate every 6 months (STANDARD-PRACTICE: acid cleaning every 3 months).  
- Cost: Comparable (STANDARD-PRACTICE: sensor replacement + chemical treatment).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- Protocol: Monitor flow rate and pressure drop across pump for 90 days post-coating.  
- Instruments: Existing flow meter and pressure transducer (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated telemetry).  
- Pass/fail: Flow rate reduction <5% (CALCULATED: baseline flow rate per stated production specs).  
- Kill criterion: Mechanism falsified if flow rate drops by >10% within 90 days.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Flow rate (stated in problem as scaling symptom). Secondary indicator: Pressure drop (supplements flow rate).  

DESIGN_POINT  
Pump internals coated with 50-μm-thick SLIPS layer, reducing silica adhesion energy by >90% at 150°C (ASSUMPTION: thermal stability from silicone oil datasheet).  

EPO PROBLEM-SOLUTION BIND  
(a) CLOSEST PRIOR ART: Standard practice uses epoxy coatings to reduce surface roughness, but silica still adheres chemically.  
(b) DISTINGUISHING FEATURE: SLIPS maintains a dynamic lubricant layer that physically repels silica particles.  
(c) OBJECTIVE TECHNICAL PROBLEM: Eliminates nucleation sites to prevent scale initiation.  
(d) WHY OBVIOUS KNOB FAILS: Smoother surfaces (epoxy) still allow silica bonding; only a liquid barrier disrupts adhesion physics.
